ecu_aps.label: Throttle
ecu_aps.note: 2026-10-21: range widened from [0, 100]. The pedal channel reads 104-106 % at full throttle on every development session (pedal / ECU calibration over-range, not a fault); with [0, 100] the in-range share fell below channel_quality_gates.failed_below on 7 of 14 sessions (NBR 20, 29, 46, 54, 63, 69, Le Castellet 32: 0.36-0.47), corner_analysis treated the throttle as missing and every entry_1_brake phase was zero-length (thesis_notes 'Phase segmentation against the chair basis', 2026-10-21). 110 covers the observed maximum (106.0) with margin; a value above it is still out of range.

log_dms_dam_fl.label: Damper Force FL
log_dms_dam_fl.note: Damper/pushrod strain-gauge force sensor, config-driven mapping added for GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt (modules/wheel_loads.py). Range gate is a plausibility bound on pushrod force for this car (order of magnitude a few kN, generous both ways) -- NOT a sensor spec; deliberately wide enough to admit a real dynamic excursion while still failing a grossly corrupted channel (see log_dms_dam_fr's own note on this file's known-bad FR reading).

log_dms_dam_fr.label: Damper Force FR
log_dms_dam_fr.note: Same channel family as log_dms_dam_fl. On GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt this specific channel reads a constant, wildly implausible value (~-15.95 million N, verified by direct sampling across the full session) -- a stuck/faulted sensor, not real data. This range gate deliberately fails that channel's quality (channel_quality_gates.failed_below), forcing modules/wheel_loads.py's per-corner static-split fallback for FR on this file, rather than silently consuming the fault value.

ecu_B_tc_act.label: TC Active
ecu_B_tc_act.note: Traction-control activity flag (clean boolean, the mechanism is real but fired on only 3 samples in the whole GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt session, a session-data limitation not a channel-quality one). Read by modules/setup_engine.py (tc_activity): a traction-limited exit ranks tc_lon above the differential (2026-10-22; was the retired decision frame's intervention evidence).

log_abs_pos.label: ABS Map Position (logged)
log_abs_pos.note: 2026-09-18: the TRUSTED ABS switch-position channel (user decision) -- resolves the cross-domain disagreement found in the damper-channel survey. Census on GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt (verified directly, not recalled): log_abs_pos/log_rt_abs_pos/stw_rt04_abs all read a constant 5 all session (dash/steering-wheel domain, mutually agreeing); abs_switch_pos reads a constant 6 (ECU domain) for the SAME session and is NOT trusted per this decision. Range [0,11] matches car_data.json's own abs table's real row count (0=Off through 11=monsoon emergency). Re-added 2026-10-23 (work order 4e item 8): modules/setup_state.py reads the current ABS map from it (session mode), since the setup sheet has no ABS field.

corner_detection.brake_throttle_max_pct_derived_from: Tier B, value predates the records. The lift-off construction at 95 (last sample at or above it before turn-in = end of full throttle) was verified on 2026-08-20 against brake pressure on Dubai, 56 corner instances: brake-pressure rise after the lift-off point median 0.135 s front / 0.130 s rear, 0 % negative, n 36 (thesis_notes 'entry_1_brake phase-boundary bug'). The construction is verified; the value 95 itself is not derived (author ruling 2026-10-21).
corner_detection.steering_unwind_fraction_derived_from: Tier B, no derivation: exit_4 ends where the post-apex steering has unwound to half its post-apex peak -- the midpoint of the unwinding. Declared 2026-10-21 (author ruling), listed as a limitation in PRODUCTION.md 12.
corner_detection.lap_time_representative_factor_derived_f: 2026-09-03, corner canonicalisation fix. Representative laps cluster within ~1% of the session's fastest valid lap on both real sessions checked (Dubai worst ratio 1.0044, v3 worst representative ratio 1.0097, lap 6); the one excluded outlier observed (v3 lap 9, an on-track incident) sits at ratio 1.097141. SWEPT and confirmed, not just argued: v3's corner count is exactly 17 for every tested factor in (1.0097, 1.097141) -- the transition happens precisely between 1.0971 (17 corners, lap 9 still excluded) and 1.0972 (20 corners, lap 9 now included) -- so the result is not just 'roughly insensitive', it is provably constant on that entire open interval by construction (the filter depends only on the derived representative-lap SET, which is a step function of the factor with steps exactly at each lap's own ratio). Re-examine this factor if a session produces a genuinely intermediate lap (e.g. a traffic-compromised lap around ratio 1.04) -- that case is unobserved in the data checked so far.

channel_corrections._comment: Decoding offsets for known-corrupt channels, applied in csv_parser before the quality/range gate. Not a zero calibration (that's wheel_loads.pushrod_offset_*_N). Applied only if the file's raw mean for the channel is inside precondition_mean_range -- a healthy export stays untouched. [2026-10-03: three offset classes now exist -- decoding faults (this block, e.g. v3 FR), event-specific logger zero entries (event_zero_entries, applied right after this block), and the static gauge-check calibration (wheel_loads.pushrod_offset_*_N, after the gate).]

log_dms_dam_fr.derived_from: GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt gauge forensics (2026-09-04) found log_dms_dam_fr carries real, correctly-signed pushrod-force signal (whole-session std=1864.2N, matching the three healthy corners' own 1925.9/2082.5/2007.3N) riding on a stationary corrupted additive offset (whole-session raw mean -15949976.44N) -- pure rescaling (x1e-3/x1e-6) was ruled out since the raw fluctuation is ALREADY at the correct physical scale. 2026-09-18: the offset was anchored empirically once a real per-outing weighing existed: K is chosen so FR's own straight-line raw mean, scaled by the tiny FR/FL static-weight ratio from the outing's real corner weighing (298.9/300.3 kg), matches FL's own straight-line raw mean -- FR is FL's own axle mate, sharing the same motion-ratio table and (per that weighing) nearly equal static load. VALIDATED against the full wheel_loads.py decomposition chain (diagnostics/inspect_deepening_phase2_fr_correction.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22)): straight-line total load +10.77% vs session weight (matches the already-recorded, aero-explained +11.64% v3 finding from when FR was on static fallback); corr(ay,Fz_fr)=+0.893, corr(ay,Fz_fl)=-0.903 (both strong, correctly signed, close to this project's own healthy-corner reference band +0.966/-0.893 to -0.895); FR/FL straight-line static means within 2-3% of the outing's own real corner weights on BOTH corners equally (a shared aero-lift bias, not an FR-specific error) -- FL/FR ratio 0.9970 vs the weighing's own 1.0047 (0.77% apart). One clean pass, no red flags -- FR promoted from the axle-total reconstruction fallback to a live, damper-measured Level 4 corner on this file.

event_zero_entries._comment: Event-specific logger zero entries (Q-CAL-2, author rulings 2026-10-03). A gauge zeroed against a different reference at one event reads a constant offset there; csv_parser subtracts zero_N from the raw channel BEFORE the quality/range gate (the gate otherwise fails the channel and wheel_loads drops to the static split). An entry applies to a file only if (a) the header's TrackName and logger serial (SystemDetails 'Serial Number') match, and (b) GATE-WINDOW GUARD: the channel's raw mean minus zero_N lies inside that channel's own range gate in 'channels' -- no new tunable; a gauge re-zeroed at a later event of the same track fails the guard and stays on the static split instead of silently taking a wrong entry. Accuracy: wheel loads from a corrected channel are 'L4 with an L2 zero' (L4-rel): logged sensor + motion-ratio table (L4), zero entry an event measurement pinned through the same car's Paul Ricard zero (L2, per-corner u below).
event_zero_entries._procedure: How an event gets its entry (documented, not automated): (1) census the event's files -- header track / serial, raw damper level vs the range gate; (2) preferred: the team's static zero check at the event, entered as a measured zero; otherwise the R3 rule of diagnostics/inspect_recover_rr.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22) -- per file and corner, the gauge-vs-raw-voltage map offset (Input 21 / 29 / 31 / 39 Voltage -> FL / FR / RL / RR, inventory maps of diagnostics/inspect_v4_windows.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22)) minus the same car's Paul Ricard map offset, median over the event's files; (3) acceptance: u <= 700 N wheel and V1-V4 on all files of the event; (4) enter the medians with file spread and u. inspect_recover_rr.py is hard-wired to the 16 NBR files, so step (2) needs that script generalised for a new event. LIMITATION (author ruling 3): the header carries no date, so two events of the same track and logger whose zeros are near-identical (both passing the guard) cannot be told apart -- recorded, not solved; an engineer-entered event id is deferred to UI work.

NBR_221.derived_from: Q-RECOVER-2 R3, 2026-10-03 (diagnostics/inspect_recover_rr.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22), author-ruled reference, recover.json): the NBR event's damper gauges were zeroed against a different reference than every other event of this car (zero entry about +43 kN vs about -15.5 kN). zero_N per corner = median over the 16 NBR files of (NBR gauge-vs-voltage map offset - the same car's Paul Ricard map offset), the Paul Ricard reference = mean of v3 and pr_us_v2; u_wheel_N = sqrt((MR x sqrt(SD^2 + e_PR^2))^2 + 98^2), dominated by the Paul Ricard zero residual e_PR. V1-V4 pass on all 16 files (Q-RECOVER-2). Config corner weights are a guideline (rule 0). FR COUPLING: the FR entry was referenced to the Paul Ricard FR map offset INCLUDING the channel_corrections log_dms_dam_fr value (+15,954,360 N); if that correction is ever re-derived, this FR entry must be re-derived with it (the two never act on the same file -- the correction's mean-range precondition cannot match NBR).
